title: At most $n^{2\alpha}$ near-minimum cuts
statement: Let $G$ be a multigraph with $n$ vertices, and let $\alpha$ and $m$ be natural numbers with $\alpha \ge 1$ and $2\alpha \le n$. If, as an inequality of real numbers, $m \cdot \binom{n}{2\alpha}^{-1} \le 1$, then $m \le n^{2\alpha}$.
hypotheses_covered: G is a multigraph whose vertex count is n
the parameter alpha is a positive natural number
caveat: The Lean treats the cut count m (numCuts) as an abstract natural number constrained only by the given inequality; the reading of m as the number of $\alpha$-approximate minimum cuts of $G$ is the intended interpretation, not part of the formal statement.
replaced:
Let $\alpha > 0$ with $2\alpha \le n = \abs{V(G)}$. If a family of $\mathrm{numCuts}$
$\alpha$-minimum cuts satisfies
$\mathrm{numCuts} \cdot \binom{n}{2\alpha}^{-1} \le 1$, then
\[
  \mathrm{numCuts} \le n^{2\alpha} .
\]
